subject.title: [Google Antigravity Ban] Frequent Tool Schema Reloading Causes False Positive Anti-Abuse Detection

question: Should OpenClaw land a bounded internal cache for provider-normalized tool schema parameters on the embedded attempt path, and what invalidation boundary should it use?
rationale: The source-level repeated-normalization path is clear, but the permanent cache boundary affects provider hooks, plugin runtime lifecycle, custom provider behavior, and the prepared-runtime migration direction.

options.title: Refresh the narrow cache PR
options.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR, cache only schema parameters for safe bundled normalizers, and keep tool objects, closures, approval state, and custom hooks per turn.

options.title: Defer to prepared runtime
options.body: Keep this issue open until the broader prepared-runtime migration carries enough provider and tool facts to avoid a separate cache layer.

options.title: Require live proof first
options.body: Hold implementation until current-main Google/Gemini or heap evidence proves the user-visible impact is still present.

recommendation.title: Refresh the narrow cache PR
recommendation.body: Refresh or replace the open cache PR, cache only schema parameters for safe bundled normalizers, and keep tool objects, closures, approval state, and custom hooks per turn.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and provider-family hook history put Vincent Koc closest to the provider/runtime code path that would own the cache boundary.
